title: Remember the Sabbath
kjv_text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.
summary: Mandates a weekly work stoppage for the whole household economy — children, servants, livestock, and resident foreigners included — grounded in God's rest after creation.
original_audience: Israelite householders, who controlled whether dependents and animals rested.
immediate_context: Fourth commandment, the hinge between duties to God and duties to neighbor; the longest commandment, with the only creation-based rationale (Deut 5:15 gives a different one — the Exodus).
historical_context: A seven-day rest cycle detached from lunar phases is without clear ancient Near Eastern parallel and became Israel's signature institution. Numbers 15:32-36 shows enforcement: a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath is stoned. The commandment is notably humane toward labor and notably lethal toward violators.
exceptions: Priestly temple labor proceeds (Matt 12:5); later rabbinic principle that saving life overrides the Sabbath; Jesus adds healing and need (Mark 2:23-28).
nt_passages: Mark 2:27 — 'The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath'
Matthew 12:1-14 — Jesus defends Sabbath healing and gleaning
Colossians 2:16 — let no man judge you regarding sabbaths
Romans 14:5 — every day alike, let each be persuaded

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it necessary to keep the Sabbath? Capital enforcement (Ex 31:14) vs. Colossians 2:16 and Romans 14:5 releasing believers from sabbath judgment.
Which day? The USofC enforces Sunday, but the commandment's seventh day is Saturday — the regime criminalizes the calendar it inherited.

usofc_implementation: The National Sabbath Act: total commercial shutdown Saturday sundown to Sunday sundown ('the Bridged Sabbath,' a denominational compromise that satisfied no one). The BSO issues Sabbath Exemption Licenses by criticality tier — hospitals Tier 1, power grid Tier 2, professional football Tier 3 after the largest lobbying campaign in USofC history. Household compliance is presumed but neighbor-reportable.
constitutional_analogue: Blue laws taken to their limit; McGowan v. Maryland (1961) upheld Sunday closing on secular grounds — the USofC deleted the secular fig leaf.
scene_ideas: An ER admitting clerk deciding at 11:58 p.m. whether an injury is 'life-threatening' or 'Monday-treatable.'
A BSO inspector timing a farmer's cows to determine whether the milking robot constitutes the cattle working.
The annual Exemption License auction — officially an 'ordered stewardship allocation' — where criticality tiers are openly bought.
satirical_uses: The football exemption: the regime found stoning a stick-gatherer scriptural but Sunday kickoff non-negotiable.
Enforcement agents work every Sabbath, covered by a standing auto-renewed exemption no one has re-read in years.
bureaucratic_uses: Sabbath Exemption License with criticality tiers and renewal fees
